title: Kernel discipline: crypto2dev_register_provider takes non-const pointer enabling post-registration writes
description: crypto2dev_register_provider() (crypto2dev_provider.h:450, registry.c:45) takes a 'struct crypto2dev_provider *p' (non-const). After registration, the provider struct's fields (name, is_fips, algos, num_algos, owner) are read by lookup and aggregate functions while holding only provider_lock for reads — there is no write-side protection against the provider module modifying these fields post-registration. The framework mutates p->list during registration (INIT_LIST_HEAD + list_add_tail), which requires non-const, but no other fields should change after registration. The API comment says 'Do not modify any field after registration' but the type system does not enforce this. A provider module with a bug that writes to is_fips or num_algos post-registration creates an unprotected data race visible to all concurrent lookups. Fix: split the struct so the list_head linkage is in a separate framework-internal struct, allowing the provider-facing fields to be declared const *; alternatively, document the constraint explicitly in the struct definition and add a BUILD_BUG_ON check for the mutable fields at registration time.
